# Flash Physical Layer Behavioral Specification

## 1. Overview

The flash physical layer is the wrapper between the flash macro and the rest of the system. It provides two independent command paths:

- A host-facing read path used for direct, low-latency reads of data-flash contents.
- A controller-facing path used for controller-initiated read, program, page erase, bank erase, and erase-suspend operations.

The physical layer must route each operation to the correct flash bank, preserve the required response order, apply or bypass scrambling and ECC according to the transaction attributes, and report completion, data, and error status back to the requesting side.

The module must support multiple flash banks. Bank selection is derived from the address supplied with each operation. Host operations and controller operations each select their target bank from their own address inputs.

---

## 2. Host Read Path

### 2.1 Capabilities

The host path is read-only. It must not issue program or erase operations. Host accesses target the data partition only; accesses to information partitions are not possible through the host path.

The host path may accept a new read before a previous read has completed. Therefore, it must track the order in which host reads are accepted and return the responses in that same order.

### 2.2 Acceptance

A host read must be accepted only when all of the following conditions are true:

- The addressed bank can accept another outstanding read.
- The response-ordering queue has room for another entry.
- The read is actually requested.

When a read is accepted, its target bank identity must be recorded at the tail of the response-ordering queue.

A host read must not be accepted to a bank whose response storage is still occupied by an earlier read to that bank. This ensures that every accepted read has a place to store its response when it completes.

### 2.3 Completion Ordering

Each bank may complete a read independently. A read from a later bank may finish before a read from an earlier bank. When this happens, the later response must be held until all earlier host reads have been returned.

The physical layer must return host read completions strictly in the order the reads were accepted. A completion is presented only when:

- The next entry in the response-ordering queue corresponds to a bank whose response is ready.

At completion, the module must provide the read data and an error indication for that transaction. The completed entry is then removed from the ordering queue, and the bank response storage is freed.

The host completion indication must be a single-cycle pulse. After a completion, a new host read may be accepted in the same cycle if acceptance conditions are met.

---

## 3. Controller Operation Path

### 3.1 Supported Operations

The controller path must support:

- Reads.
- Programs.
- Page erases.
- Bank erases.
- Erase suspend requests.

Controller operations may target either data or information partitions. The controller supplies the partition and information-select attributes needed to distinguish the target.

### 3.2 Routing

Each controller operation must be routed to the bank selected by its address. The module must not merge or reorder operations from different banks.

Controller operations use the controller-supplied attributes for scrambling, ECC, high-endurance mode, program type, last-word indication, and address/data keys. These attributes must be forwarded to the addressed bank.

### 3.3 Completion

The module must return the appropriate completion indication for the selected operation type:

- Read completion with read data and read error status.
- Program completion.
- Erase completion.

Controller operations are treated as non-pipelined. The controller interface holds an operation until its completion is returned. Therefore, the physical layer must not need to reorder controller responses.

Erase suspend requests must be forwarded to the addressed bank. The eventual completion of the suspended or resumed erase operation is reported through the normal erase completion mechanism.

---

## 4. Arbitration Between Host and Controller

When a host read and a controller operation target the same bank at the same time, the host read must be given priority.

The controller must not be starved by continuous host traffic. If the controller repeatedly loses arbitration, its priority must be raised so that it is eventually granted access. This applies independently to each bank.

Host reads that cannot be accepted because their bank response storage is full must be suppressed, even if the bank itself could otherwise accept a read.

---

## 5. Address and Region Attribute Handling

For host reads, the physical layer must determine whether the addressed page belongs to a configured data-flash memory-protection region. The selected region configuration determines whether scrambling and ECC are enabled for the host read.

The region selection must follow the memory-protection region priority rules. If no region matches, or if the matching region is not enabled, the host read must be treated as non-scrambled and non-ECC.

Region attributes are used only for host read scrambling and ECC behavior. They must not be used to grant or deny host access; access permission enforcement is handled outside the physical layer.

Controller operations do not use these region-derived attributes. They use the explicit scrambling and ECC attributes supplied by the controller.

---

## 6. Scrambling and ECC Behavior

### 6.1 Read Scrambling

When a read transaction targets an address with scrambling enabled, the data read from the flash macro must be descrambled before it is returned to the requester.

When scrambling is disabled, the raw data read from the flash macro must be returned without descrambling.

Scrambling must be applied consistently for both host reads and controller reads, according to the applicable attributes.

### 6.2 Program Scrambling

When a program transaction targets an address with scrambling enabled, the program data must be scrambled before it is stored in the flash macro.

When scrambling is disabled, the program data must be stored without scrambling.

### 6.3 ECC

The physical layer must support integrity protection on stored flash data. Read data must be checked, and a failed integrity check must be reported as a read error to the requesting side.

The physical layer must also support optional reliability ECC. When enabled:

- Single-bit errors must be corrected.
- A correctable-error indication must be reported.
- The address associated with the corrected error must be reported.
- Uncorrectable errors must be reported as read errors.

When reliability ECC is disabled, the corresponding protection is not applied, and reads behave according to the non-ECC path.

### 6.4 Program Data Integrity

Program data supplied by the controller must be checked for integrity before being committed to the flash macro. If a program-data integrity check fails, the program operation must be treated as failed and must not store the invalid data.

---

## 7. Read Caching

Each flash bank may maintain a small read cache to avoid repeated flash-macro accesses for recently read words.

The cache must store de-scrambled data, so a read hit can be served without another flash-macro access.

The module must invalidate cache entries when they are affected by a program or erase:

- A page erase or program must invalidate entries in the affected page.
- A bank erase must invalidate all entries in the affected bank.

Read caching must be enabled or disabled according to the controller’s read-buffer-enable command. When disabled, every read must access the flash macro rather than being served from the cache.

---

## 8. Life-Cycle, Debug, and BIST Gating

The physical layer must synchronize life-cycle non-volatile debug enable indications before using them.

### 8.1 JTAG

Access to the flash macro’s JTAG interface must be allowed only when non-volatile debug is enabled by life cycle.

When non-volatile debug is disabled:

- JTAG clock, data input, and mode select stimulus must be gated off.
- The JTAG serial data output must not be driven with flash-macro data.

When non-volatile debug is enabled, the JTAG interface must be allowed to operate normally.

### 8.2 BIST

Flash built-in self-test enable must be allowed only when non-volatile debug is enabled.

When non-volatile debug is disabled, the BIST enable must be forced inactive regardless of the external BIST request.

---

## 9. Vendor Flash Test, Scan, Power, and Observation Interfaces

The physical layer must provide direct paths for the following vendor-flash control and observation functions:

- Scan enable, scan mode, and scan reset.
- Flash power-down and power-ready indications.
- Bidirectional flash test-mode and test-voltage connections.
- Flash observation controls and observation outputs.
- Vendor-flash register access through a system bus interface.

The physical layer must not alter scan, test, or power-control behavior. These functions belong to the flash macro and must reach it unchanged.

Vendor-flash register accesses must be passed to the flash macro, and the resulting response must be returned to the requestor.

---

## 10. Status Reporting

The physical layer must report the following status to the controller:

- Flash macro initialization busy status.
- Available program types.
- Read completion status with read data and read error.
- Program completion status.
- Erase completion status.
- Correctable ECC error status and associated address.
- Aggregate error status for program-integrity failures, storage-integrity failures, reliability-integrity failures, internal FSM errors, and unsolicited acknowledgments.

These status signals must be based on the target bank selected by the controller operation.

For status that is common across all banks, the module must report the value as long as any bank reports the condition.

Fatal alerts from the flash macro must be propagated to the alert output and reported to the controller.

---

## 11. Reset and Disable Behavior

On reset:

- All response-ordering state must be cleared.
- No host read completions may be presented.
- No controller operation completions may be presented.
- The module must not accept new operations until reset is released.

When flash access is disabled:

- New host reads and new controller operations must not be issued to the flash macro.
- Program or erase operations already in progress must be allowed to complete.
- The module must report the disabled state to the banking logic so that no new transactions are started.

After a disable condition is asserted, the host and controller paths must not begin new flash operations until the disable is deasserted or the module is reset.
